title: ECoG speech neuroprosthesis with avatar restores 78-words-per-minute communication after brainstem stroke (UCSF)
summary: 253-electrode ECoG and deep-learning decoder let Ann Johnson, mute since a 2005 stroke, produce text, synthesized speech and an avatar
account: At UCSF Medical Center, a 47-year-old woman with quadriplegia and anarthria from a pontine infarct in 2005 (named in news reports as Ann Johnson) had a 253-channel electrocorticography array implanted over speech cortical areas in September 2022 under the BRAVO trial (NCT03698149). Deep-learning recurrent neural networks trained on her attempted silent speech decoded text at a median 78 words per minute with 25% median word error rate over a 1,024-word vocabulary, synthesized speech personalised to her pre-injury voice, and animated a facial avatar (Metzger et al., Nature, 23 August 2023). She had earlier communicated by letterboard. The paper anchors the text-decoding result to 14 days of data collection shortly after the September 2022 implant and gives no calendar session dates, so the implant month (1 September 2022) is used as the observation date.
purpose: Built to restore communication by decoding attempted speech from cortical surface recordings into text, synthesized speech and avatar animation; that was the intended benefit and is what occurred.
model_version: 253-channel high-density ECoG array; bidirectional RNN decoders with CTC loss producing text, synthesized speech and avatar gestures; 1,024-word vocabulary
developer: UCSF Chang Lab with UC Berkeley
taxonomy_note: Filed as benefit created or restored on the strength of an individually observed outcome for a named beneficiary; the event is a research-session demonstration (the cited NPR report says the systems only work in the lab), not an everyday deployment, which is why it is not filed as a category-3 accuracy study.

ratings.reason: Material benefit to one identifiable person: fast text, synthesized voice and avatar communication demonstrated in research sessions (run at her residence); the paper reports no independent use outside those sessions, so it is not rated life-changing.

ai_role.statement: Deep-learning decoders are the mechanism: they map cortical activity during attempted speech to phonemes, speech units and articulatory gestures, and every output (text, voice, avatar) depends on them.

echoes.setting: UCSF, a clinical trial participant with severe paralysis and anarthria (the accessible abstract does not say whether this is the same participant and the full text is behind a login wall, so the identity is unverified): continuously streaming speech synthesis personalised to the participant's pre-injury voice in 80 ms increments
